Yes, for most everyday spenders and first-year savers, Chase UK beats Monzo on both cashback and savings. However, Chase's best perks come with strict monthly conditions, and its easy-access savings rate drops significantly after your first year.   
Abel
+ 1

Side-by-Side Comparison
Feature	Chase UK (Free Account)	Monzo (Free Account)
Monthly Fee	£0	£0 (Paid plans: Extra £3, Perks £9, Max £19/mo)
Cashback Structure	2% flat on everyday essentials (capped at £20/mo)	Offer-based (typically 2%–10% at selected partner retailers)
Cashback Rules	Must keep £1,000+ in Chase savers every day & make 15+ payments in the prior month	Must manually activate specific retailer offers in the app before spending
Easy-Access Savings	4.75% AER variable for new customers (12 months), then 2.50% AER	2.80% AER (Instant Access) or 3.45% AER (Select Access, £500 min)
Paid-Plan Savings	N/A	Up to 3.80% AER Instant Access on Monzo Max (£19/mo)
Regular Saver / Fixed	6.50% AER fixed for 12 months (up to £300/mo) + 5.00% AER Round-ups	Up to 5.25% AER on 3-year Fixed Pots & Cash ISAs (£500 min)
1. Cashback: Predictable Essentials vs. Retailer Offers

Chase UK wins for routine spending: You earn 2% cashback (up to £20/month, or £240/year) across broad everyday categories: UK groceries, restaurants, cafes, takeaways, everyday transport, fuel, and public EV charging.   
Money Saving Expert

The Catch: After an initial grace period when you join, you only unlock cashback if you make at least 15 card or Direct Debit payments and hold at least £1,000 across your Chase saver accounts every single day of the previous calendar month. (Note: Direct Debits count toward the 15-payment target, though they don't earn cashback themselves.)   
Chase UK
+ 1

Monzo is hit-or-miss: Monzo doesn't offer blanket category cashback. Instead, you opt into rotating merchant-specific deals in the app (e.g., certain supermarkets, coffee chains, or fashion retailers). It can yield higher percentages on one-off purchases, but you won't earn consistently on everyday bills or local shops.   
Abel

2. Savings: Strong First Year vs. Long-Term Flexibility

Chase UK wins in Year 1 and for monthly savers: New Chase customers who open a Boosted Saver within 31 days get 4.75% AER (variable, including a 2.25% 12-month fixed bonus) on up to £1 million. Chase also offers a penalty-free 6.50% AER Regular Saver (up to £300/month) and 5.00% AER on spare-change round-ups.   
Chase UK
+ 1

The Catch: Once your 12-month boost expires, Chase's standard easy-access rate drops to 2.50% AER (tracking 1.50% below the Bank of England base rate).   
DepositScout

Monzo wins for Cash ISAs, fixed terms, and post-Year 1 easy access: On a free Monzo plan, the standard Instant Access Pot (2.80% AER) slightly edges out Chase's unboosted rate, and Monzo's Select Access Pot pays 3.45% AER (with a £500 minimum and withdrawal limits). Monzo also offers Cash ISAs (from 2.80% instant access up to 5.25% fixed) and multi-year fixed pots, whereas Chase UK does not currently offer ISAs or fixed-term bonds.   
DepositScout

Which should you choose?

Pick Chase UK if you have at least £1,000 in savings to park there and regularly spend on groceries, dining, or commuting. Even after the first-year savings boost ends, earning £10–£20/month in cashback easily outweighs the small interest difference on that £1,000 balance.

Pick Monzo if you want tax-free Cash ISAs, prefer keeping less than £1,000 in savings, or want Monzo's superior budgeting tools (like Salary Sorter and bill-splitting Pots) without worrying about monthly transaction quotas. Many UK savers use Monzo as their main bills/budgeting hub and Chase strictly as a daily spending and savings card.   
Abel
